correctness.rationale: Each proper geodesic convex tree halfspace is an oriented single-edge cut. For n=8 a depth-four complete tree must split all 16 concepts 8/8 then 4/4: querying v and then w forces distance d(v,w)=4, and a subsequent balanced query among full plus three off-path cuts forces distance two to the path. Conversely queries v,w yield four exact four-concept cells; query x on the equal-answer cells and a middle path vertex on the mixed cells to split each 2/2; distinct concepts separate on final queries. Lower rank3 for all n>=4 follows from a four-vertex subtree; n<=7 hits cardinality cap. Path formula follows balanced threshold chains. Exact labeled and shape census replayed exhaustively in embedded Python; no finite-to-infinite inference.

value.rationale: The eight-vertex boundary is the first place where the natural 2n-hypothesis information bound can be strict, and its attainability has a sharp geometric if-and-only-if classification rather than an ad hoc finite invariant. The complete 23-type census quantifies the obstruction and the all-order path formula provides an extremal reference family. This distinguishes adaptive shattering on graph convex cuts from previously studied active query complexity and VC/Radon bounds. Numerical census supports the structural theorem; no inflated general classification or novelty of elementary threshold search is claimed.
